title: Security review - Data residency & region pinning
summary: High-level security review focused on data residency and region pinning for Acme Health. Discussed options for pinning inference requests to US or EU regions, cross-border processing concerns, list of sub-processors (cloud providers), encryption/KMS options, audit log retention and export, and attestation artifacts (SOC 2 / ISO). Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 report, DPA and subprocessors list, propose pilot with EU-pinned deployment and run small benchmark; SE to scope technical configs for KMS and audit-logging retention.
topics: Encryption at rest and in transit / KMS/HSM
next_steps: Alicia to send SOC 2 report and DPA links (by 2026-02-23)
Marco to prepare technical note on KMS integration and key custody options (by 2026-02-25)
Schedule pilot for EU region-pinned Dedicated capacity (target start 2026-03-09)
Customer to confirm list of regulated datasets and residency requirements (by 2026-02-27)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start time: 15:00 PST / 23:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (CISO, Acme Health), Liam O'Connor (Product), Dr. Emily Zhao (Head of ML)

Summary: quick security deep dive on region pinning/data residency, clarifying cross-border processing, subprocessors, and KMS options.

00:00 - Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alicia from Redwood, AE on the account, with Marco from our SE team.
00:12 - Sara: Hi Alicia, hi Marco, thanks. Im Sara, CISO at Acme Health. Well focus on data residency and legal constraints, especially EU patient data.
00:28 - Marco: Great, thanks Sara. Quick agenda: region pinning, cross-border processing, sub-processors, encryption/KMS, audit logging and retention, and artifacts we can share like SOC 2.
00:45 - Liam: That works for us. Our legal team is worried about any offshoring and the subprocessors list.
01:02 - Alicia: Totally. At a high level Redwood supports pinned routing so requests can be served entirely from a single region—US or EU—and we have Dedicated and Private options for stronger isolation.
01:20 - Sara: When you say "served entirely from EU" does that include model weights, KV cache, and backups? We can’t have replicas leaving the region for certain datasets.
01:40 - Marco: Good question. For our Dedicated EU offering we can ensure model serving, KV cache, and persistent storage for that tenant remain in EU datacenters. Backups can be configured to stay in-region or customer-managed. There are a few details around telemetry and control-plane metadata which usually cross regions—happy to walk through that.
02:05 - Sara: Telemetry is a big one. If control-plane telemetry includes identifiers that could be considered personal, legal needs to know.
02:20 - Marco: Right. By default control-plane telemetry is minimized and scrubbed; for regulated customers we route control-plane metadata through the customer's VPC or use Private deployments. Also we support options to obfuscate request identifiers.
02:41 - Dr. Emily: From an ML perspective we’re also concerned about model variants falling back to a US-hosted cheaper variant and that causing cross-border processing. Do you have fallback behaviors pinned?
02:58 - Alicia: We do. Fallbacks are policy-driven. For EU-pinned customers we can require strict region-only fallbacks and deny cross-region failovers unless customer toggles a cross-border exception.
03:16 - Sara: Good. What about subprocessors—cloud providers like AWS and GCP, or other third parties? We need the full list and locations.
03:35 - Marco: Our primary cloud partners for EU Dedicated are AWS EU-West and GCP europe-west. We can provide the subprocessors list and the datacenter regions we use. We also use CDNs and monitoring vendors—those are listed in the subprocessor manifest we can share.
03:58 - Liam: Do you use any US-based analytics vendors that could access logs?
04:10 - Marco: Some telemetry ingestion and our control plane live in our hosted control plane which may use US-based services; for Private/VPC deployments we can keep control-plane pieces in customer-managed infra.
04:28 - Sara: That suggests we might need Private deploy or a Dedicated EU with VPC egress restrictions.
04:44 - Alicia: Exactly, many regulated customers pick Dedicated EU with strict routing and a DPA that includes region pinning obligations.
04:58 - Marco: On encryption: data in transit is TLS, at rest we use AES-256. For key management we support Redwood-managed KMS as well as customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or external HSMs. If you need full key custody, we recommend customer-managed keys and we can document the KMS flow.
05:22 - Dr. Emily: If the keys are customer-managed, does inference latency increase due to KMS calls on token generation or model loading?
05:36 - Marco: There is a small initial overhead for key retrieval during setup, but runtime tokenization and inference paths use cached keys and do not call KMS per request. We have best-practice patterns in the KMS note I’ll share.
05:56 - Sara: Audit logs: how long do you retain request logs and how granular are they? We need 7 years for some audit trails but we can maybe export to our SEIM.
06:09 - Marco: By default audit logs are retained 90 days in the console; we offer extended retention as an add-on and you can stream logs to your SIEM (syslog/forwarding or S3 export). We also support per-tenant retention policies.
06:30 - Liam: Can we export raw request payloads to our internal storage? We'd prefer to keep PII in-house and only store non-sensitive traces in Redwood.
06:45 - Alicia: Yes, you can opt out of request payload retention. We have flags to disable storing request bodies; only metadata retained. We also have redact-at-ingest rules.
07:03 - Sara: About GDPR and cross-border: does Redwood rely on SCCs, BCRs, or something else?
07:18 - Marco: We provide SCCs as part of the DPA. For some enterprise customers we can discuss binding corporate rules depending on contract. We’ll include the legal team in follow-up if you need custom wording.
07:35 - Liam: If we want EU-only training data for fine-tuning, can that process stay inside the EU?
07:50 - Marco: Yes—fine-tuning and any model training can be pinned to EU infra, but we need to lock down checkpoints and artifact stores to ensure there’s no cross-region replication.
08:06 - Dr. Emily: Any limits around running long-context inference in EU vs US? We saw in your docs some kernels are optimized per region/hardware.
08:20 - Marco: Some newer GPU types (and optimized kernels) may be region-limited; we produce a model compatibility matrix by region. If a specific kernel isn’t available in EU, we can either provide a compatible fallback with slightly different perf characteristics or offer Dedicated hardware placement.
08:40 - Sara: Perf differences are acceptable as long as we have deterministic behavior and SLOs.
08:48 - Alicia: For compliance we typically document the expected latency and throughput for the chosen region and hardware, and include that in the Reserved Capacity contract.
09:01 - Liam: Can you describe the telemetry identifiers that leave the region? We need to evaluate if they could be considered personal data.
09:15 - Marco: Telemetry typically includes request timestamps, region, and hashed tenant id. We can provide pseudonymization options and, for Private deploys, avoid sending telemetry off-region entirely.
09:33 - Sara: What about subprocessors list—can you provide names and whether they process in US or EU?
09:44 - Marco: Yes, we have a maintained subprocessor CSV we’ll share. Includes cloud providers, monitoring, CDNs, analytics, and infra partners; each row shows region processing and data types.
10:02 - Alicia: We’ll attach the subprocessor manifest and our DPA with SCCs after the call.
10:10 - Dr. Emily: One more question on keys: do you support asymmetric key signing for model artifacts? We want to verify model provenance.
10:24 - Marco: We support signing model artifacts with customer keys in customer-managed KMS workflows; we’ll include the signing flow in the KMS note.
10:38 - Sara: Regarding SOC 2 and ISO—do you have recent reports? We need SOC 2 type II and an ISO 27001 cert summary.
10:49 - Alicia: Yes, we’ll share our latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary under NDA or via a secure link.
11:02 - Liam: For the pilot, can we have EU region pinned Dedicated capacity with logging forwarded to our S3 bucket in eu-west-1?
11:15 - Marco: Absolutely—we can set up a 2-week pilot with EU-pinned Dedicated and log forwarding to your S3. We’ll need a bucket ARN and IAM role to allow writes.
11:31 - Sara: Any risk of cross-border calls when autoscaling triggers burst capacity?
11:44 - Marco: Autoscaling respects region policies; for Dedicated EU we configure burst capacity to stay within EU pools. If EU capacity is exhausted we have explicit policy toggles—deny or allow cross-region failover. For strict compliance we set deny.
11:59 - Alicia: Quick recap of deliverables: Alicia to send SOC 2, DPA and subprocessor manifest; Marco to send KMS note and pilot plan; Sara to send list of regulated datasets; Redwood to provision EU trial.
12:18 - Sara: Sounds good. One last small item—what about personnel access? We need assurance on RBAC and SSO for your console.
12:34 - Marco: RBAC is role-based, SSO via SAML/IdP is standard; we can provide admin and read-only roles and optional MFA enforcement. For Private deployments, admin access can be restricted to your VPC and SSO directory.
12:55 - Dr. Emily: Great, thanks.
13:02 - Alicia: Thanks everyone. We’ll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
13:15 - Liam: Thanks, Alicia, Marco. Appreciate it.
13:22 - Sara: Thanks all.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-transcription of product names (e.g., "Red-wood inference" in one spot) and speaker overlaps. Links shared during call: https://redwood.ai/security (SOC 2 link placeholder), https://redwood.ai/dpa (DPA placeholder), subprocessor manifest link: https://redwood.ai/subprocessors.csv (placeholder).

End of call.
